Municipal Services 
 
The Ballyogan Regional Temporary Rest Centre opened its doors to Ukrainian nationals 
on 28 April. The Rest Centre continues to accommodate up to 300 displaced Ukrainian 
nationals for short periods. Over 3,000 people have stayed at the centre for short 
periods.  
   
As part of a comprehensive wrap around service, accommodation services at the Centre 
are being supported by HSE staff including Environmental Health, Public Health and 
COVID-19 services. The HSE is providing onsite support to meet the healthcare needs of 
Ukrainian residents, and residents also have access to an offsite GP service 7 days a 
week.   
   
Among the facilities available in the temporary rest centre is separate laundry and 
sanitary facilities, internet access, television spaces, games consoles, games room, 
chessboards, use of bikes and scooters, libraries of Ukrainian books for children and 
adults, translation services, as well as online access to Ukrainian newspapers and 
magazines.   
   
Additionally, orientation and information sessions, basic English language lessons and an 
arts and music entertainment programme is being developed both onsite and nearby 
offsite.  
   
Local coordination efforts continue to provide comprehensive support services from 
Southside Partnership, HSE, An Garda Siochána, Department of Social Protection, dlr 
Education and Training Board, TUSLA, Community and Family Resource Centres, dlr 
Volunteers Centre, colleagues in the East Region and a number of other community and 
voluntary groups.    
   
Work is now underway to provide extra facilities, including 92 extra beds, a homework 
club room for children, an adults workspace, and a new improved space for teenagers.

3. Water & Drainage 
  
Drainage and Flood Alleviation 
Engineering and Environmental Consultants were appointed in December 2019 for Flood 
Risk Management works on the Deansgrange Stream. This is a 4-to-5-year project. 
Activities completed to date include additional survey work, CCTV surveys, a Constraints 
Study, Hydrological analysis, and hydraulic modelling. Optioneering, environmental 
surveys and engagement with key stakeholders are underway. A Ground Investigation 
Contract is complete, and the report is awaited. Work has begun to review sites for 
environmental impacts. We have received preliminary approval from Irish Rail to tunnel 
under the rail line. Public Consultation on the preferred option took place on the 13th 
December. Detailed preparation is beginning for the Part 8 submission. 
 
Engineering and Environmental Consultants have also been appointed for Flood Risk 
Management Works on the Carrickmines/Shanganagh Rivers. This is a 5+ year project. 
Data gathering is underway. A Flow/Rainfall Survey is complete. Further topographical 
survey work has been done. Early damage/benefits assessments are underway to ensure 
a cost-beneficial scheme is achievable. An initial public engagement is complete following 
short briefing sessions with Area Councillors. The Hydrology/Hydraulic report is now 
complete and initial options are being developed. A Contractor was appointed for the Site 
Investigation.  The on-site SI work is largely completed. The Contractor must now 
process the information. 
 
The Monkstown environs flood risk mapping project is underway. The topographical 
survey is now largely completed. The flow/rainfall survey is now completed, and the 
CCTV survey is well underway.  Draft flood maps have been produced and reviewed. The 
consultant is also looking at some options to help relieve potential flooding in the 
catchment.

7. Dún Laoghaire Harbour 
 
Cruise Ship Business 
We had approximately 72 Cruise Ships booked into the Harbour in 2022. 3 ships 
cancelled due to weather.  Overall, the Harbour was being well received by ship 
management, cruise guests and the crew who come ashore.  We are now doing a full 
review of the 2022 season with our various stakeholders and beginning to plan for a 
busier 2023 season with approximately 90 ships booked at present.  
 
Grant Funding 
The Brexit Adjustment: Local Authority Marine Infrastructure Scheme 2022 – 2023 from 
the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine has launched a Second Tranche call 
for applications. Dun Laoghaire Harbour received over €3 million in grant funding from 
the first tranche. We submitted 5 grant applications to this scheme by the deadline of 
30th September 2022 and have been awarded another €1 million in grant funding for 
improvements on the Carlisle Pier.  
  
Projects: 
  
National Watersports Campus 
DLRCC in partnership with Irish Sailing and the Irish Underwater Council have been 
approved in principle for Stream 1 Grant funding for the development of a National 
Watersports Campus. We have responded to requests for additional information and are 
now finalising the grant process and agreements with the project partners.  An MOU has 
been signed with Irish Sailing and Diving Ireland in order to set out and agree the 
objectives of the project. 
 
DLRCC and Irish Sailing are developing a brochure/prospectus for the project to detail 
the project vision and scope. It is hoped that this initiative will assist in building 
momentum and support for the project. This document will be presented to councilors in 
February 2023.

procurement for this project. This project was tendered, and Sorensen Construction have 
been appointed to deliver the project. We are awaiting Foreshore consent to proceed to
